title: How Parkinson's Disease Spreads Through the Brain
hook: Yale scientists found two neuron surface proteins that help the toxic protein behind Parkinson's spread from cell to cell — and blocking them dramatically slowed disease progression in mice.
key_points: Yale researchers identified two neuron surface proteins involved in spreading the toxic protein linked to Parkinson's disease.
These proteins appear to help the toxic protein move from one neuron to another.
Blocking the two proteins in mice dramatically reduced disease progression.
This offers a potential new drug target for future Parkinson's therapies.
content_html: Parkinson's disease, like Alzheimer's, spreads through the brain over time — and understanding exactly how has been a key open question for researchers hoping to slow it down. Yale scientists say they've found part of the answer: two proteins sitting on the surface of neurons.
extra_html: As ScienceDaily reports, these two surface proteins appear to help the toxic protein behind Parkinson's move from one neuron to the next, spreading the damage further into the brain. When researchers blocked both proteins in mice, disease progression slowed dramatically — a strong enough effect to mark them as a genuinely promising drug target. It's a mouse study, so a human therapy is still a ways off, but finding a specific, blockable mechanism behind how the disease spreads is a meaningful step for a condition where treatment options remain limited.

related.title: How Alzheimer's Might Spread From Cell to Cell
related.hook: A common brain protein may double as a delivery vehicle for Alzheimer's, ferrying toxic tau out of damaged neurons and into healthy ones — a possible new target for slowing the disease.

related.title: Scientists May Have Found How Alzheimer's Kills Brain Cells
related.hook: Researchers say they've found a previously overlooked mechanism of brain cell death behind both Alzheimer's and frontotemporal dementia — and it might be possible to interrupt.

related.title: Keeping Your Brain Healthy
related.hook: No pill prevents dementia, but the habits that protect your heart turn out to protect your brain too.
